column2: On the authority of Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī Jurthūm ibn Nāshir (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), who said:

“Allah the Exalted has laid down obligations, so do not neglect them; He has set limits, so do not overstep them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search into them.” A ḥasan hadith.
Faraḍa (“has laid down”): has made obligatory and binding.
Farāʾiḍ (“obligations”): what Allah has made obligatory on His servants and bound them to carry out.
“So do not neglect them”: by leaving them or being careless about them until their time has passed; rather, carry them out as they have been made obligatory on you.
“He has set limits”: these are all that Allah has permitted to be done, whether by way of obligation, recommendation or permissibility.
“So do not overstep them”: do not go beyond what has been set for you by contravening what is commanded and committing what is prohibited.
“So do not violate them”: do not engage in them or approach them.
“And He has remained silent about things”: He has not ruled them obligatory, lawful or unlawful,
“out of mercy for you”: by not forbidding them, so that one would be punished for doing them, and not making them obligatory, so that one would be punished for leaving them,
“not out of forgetfulness”: of their rulings—“My Lord neither errs nor forgets” [Ṭā Hā 20:52].
“So do not search into them”: do not probe into them, for that may lead to burdensome obligations.

The division of the rulings of the religion into four categories: obligations, whose right is that they are not neglected; prohibitions, whose right is that they are not approached; limits, whose right is that they are not overstepped; and what is passed over in silence, whose right is that it is not searched into.

This gathers all the rulings of the religion, and whoever acts on it has won the reward and is safe from punishment. That is why one of the scholars said: There is no single hadith among the hadiths that on its own gathers the foundations and branches of the religion more than this hadith.
